haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: the fence read, write users, upsert the outbox row, then commit. Then the copy to Postgres is tried with a 200 ms wait. A Postgres failure never fails the request; the outbox row stays for the sweeper.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version. Equal or higher versions are never replaced.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance reports the Phase 0 build and users.dual_write at 100, outbox depth is under 1,000 with oldest entry under 60 s, and Postgres is healthy, held for two minutes. Flags can be up to 30 seconds stale.
haiku-low.q4: It checks replica lag and sleeps 5 s if lag exceeds 5 s. It reads the replica in batches of 2,000 rows by id, and runs in one worker holding a lease.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: a clean compare run, then stepped read flags (1, 10, 50, 100 percent) with 30 minutes free of errors and mismatches. Source of truth: reads at 100% on Postgres for 3 days, a clean compare within 24 h, outbox under 100, no pending erasures, Postgres healthy.
haiku-low.q6: The user_sync_outbox row, stored in MySQL during phase A. The sweeper copies it to Postgres under the version rule and deletes it only after the copy succeeds.
haiku-low.q7: Each erasure writes a tombstone in the target database first. Every copy takes the per-id lock and checks for a tombstone, so a racing copy is blocked.
haiku-low.q8: In migration_state in MySQL, as last_completed_id, set after each batch commits in Postgres. Copies are idempotent, so a repeated batch is safe. The backfill stops at an empty batch.
haiku-low.q9: Compare runs in id chunks of 2,000 find differences. Confirmed missing or lower-version rows are repaired via an outbox insert. Higher-version, field and extra-row differences are investigated, not repaired automatically. Tombstoned ids are ignored.
haiku-low.q10: MySQL owner is set to paused, so writes take the MySQL path only if owner is mysql and the Postgres path only if owner is pg. A run past 80 s aborts and restores owner mysql, unless the commit point has passed; then the resume rule finishes it.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids from its sequence, set to MySQL MAX(id)+10,000,000 at the commit point. Ids are never reused. After rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is checked and raised above MAX(id) if needed.
haiku-low.q12: A reverse sweeper copies Postgres reverse outbox rows into MySQL, keeping it current. Rollback sets read_source to 0, drains, pauses Postgres, checks, commits owner=mysql, and restarts the forward sweeper. The option ends at phase C, set after at least 14 days in phase B.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: transaction writes users plus outbox row and commits, then the request tries to copy to Postgres (waits at most 200 ms, only if users.dual_write applies). If Postgres fails or times out, the caller sees nothing: step 4 never fails the request; the outbox row stays for the sweeper.
sonnet.q2: Only if the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (version rule). Equal or higher versions are never replaced. Also blocked if a tombstone exists; the per-id lock is taken.
sonnet.q3: Backfill gate: for two continuous minutes every instance reports the Phase 0 build and app_flag_value users.dual_write = 100; outbox depth below 1,000 with oldest entry under 60 s; Postgres healthy. Flags can be up to 30 seconds stale across instances.
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica (not primary), in batches of 2,000 rows by id; if replica lag exceeds 5 s it sleeps 5 s and rechecks. It runs only when the gate is open.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill done and a clean compare run (zero confirmed mismatches); then steps 1/10/50/100% each wait for all instances to report the value plus 30 min with no new Postgres read errors or confirmed mismatches, with a person checking dashboards. Source of truth (step 9): reads_pg_since at least 3 days old; clean compare run within last 24 h; outbox depth below 100; no pending erasures; Postgres healthy.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (user_sync_outbox with user_id, version, queued_at), written in the same MySQL transaction as the change (in MySQL during phase A). The forward sweeper retries and copies it to Postgres, then deletes the row.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones in user_tombstones (in each database) block every copy, and every copy takes the per-id lock (pg advisory xact lock in Postgres; SELECT FOR SHARE on the tombstone row/gap in MySQL) and checks for a tombstone. Erasure writes the tombstone first, then deletes the copy. Compare ignores tombstoned ids.
sonnet.q8: In MySQL migration_state.last_completed_id (checkpoint and counters), set after the Postgres batch transaction commits; repeated batches are safe because copies are idempotent, and a restarted worker resumes after the checkpoint. It stops when a batch comes back empty.
sonnet.q9: The full comparison (step 6, daily through steps 7-8) in 2,000-id chunks, replica vs Postgres. It classifies: missing in Postgres, lower version in Postgres, higher version in Postgres (alert), field difference, extra in Postgres. Each is re-checked against the MySQL primary and outbox. Missing/lower-version are repaired by inserting an outbox row for the sweeper; others are investigated, not auto-repaired. Tombstoned ids are ignored.
sonnet.q10: Every write starts with a fence read of users_control in MySQL (FOR SHARE); it takes the MySQL path only if owner is mysql, the Postgres path only if owner is pg (or MySQL unreachable and the users.write_owner flag is pg). The switch pauses via owner=paused (new writes get 503, waits for in-flight writes). If it runs long, it aborts at 80 s (budget 90 s) before the commit point by restoring MySQL owner=mysql. After the commit point it always completes step 5.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids from its sequence, which at the commit point is set to MySQL MAX(id)+10,000,000. Ids are never reused. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is checked to be above MAX(id) and set if not (metadata-only in MySQL 8).
sonnet.q12: A reverse outbox in Postgres (mode pg_reverse) with a reverse sweeper that copies rows to MySQL under the version rule and tombstone check. Rollback: set read_source to 0; pre-drain; pause Postgres; drain and delta check against MySQL primary; check AUTO_INCREMENT; commit point in MySQL owner=mysql and write_owner=mysql; then Postgres owner=mysql, clear mode; stop reverse sweeper, start forward sweeper, dual_write 100. Budget 90 s. The option ends at step 11 when mode is set to pg_only (at least 14 days after pg_owner_since, reverse outbox empty).
